Rigid Grain Net (RGN)

Source: R/strain_analysis.R
RGN_plot.Rd

The rigid grain net (Jessup et al. 2007) plots the distribution of the finite strain ratio \(R\) and orientation \(\theta\) of porphyroclasts over the theoretical distribution of tailless clasts. The plot estimates the critical shape factor \(B^\ast\) marking the transition between stable-sink positions and infinitely rotating porphyroclasts. This critical shape factor is interpreted as the mean kinematic vorticity number \(W_m\).

Usage

RGN_plot(
  r,
  theta,
  angle_error = 3,
  n_iter = 2000L,
  probs = 0.975,
  p_min = 0.95,
  grid = 0.05,
  main = "Rigid-Grain-Net",
  guides = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

r

numeric. Porphyroclast aspect ratio (long axis / short axis).

theta

numeric. Angle between long axis and foliation (degrees).

angle_error

numeric. Standard deviation of the angle measurement error in degrees. 3 by default.

n_iter

integer. Number of bootstrap resamples. 2000 by default.

probs

numeric. Probability in \([0, 1]\) used to estimate the critical shape factor, i.e. the quantile of shape factors of clasts classified as outside the critical hyperbola. 0.975 by default.

p_min

numeric. Minimum probability that a clast lies outside the critical threshold for it to be used in the estimate. 0.95 by default.

grid

numeric. Spacing of hyperbolae.

main

character. The main title (on top).

guides

logical. Whether guides of the projection grid should be added to the plot. Defaults to getOption("structr.guides").

...

plotting arguments passed to graphics::points()

Value

A plot. Invisibly, a list with values (matrix of B and theta), Wm (point estimate of the critical shape factor) and Wm_CI (bootstrap percentile interval).

Details

The Mean Kinematic Vorticity Number

The mean kinematic vorticity number \(W_m\) is estimated as the upper probs quantile of the shape factor \(B^\ast\) of clasts that lie outside the critical hyperbola (Jessup et al. 2007, Eq. 1, evaluated at \(W_m = B^\ast\)).

The orientation \(\theta\) of the porphyroclast long axis relative to the foliation is given by $$\theta = \frac{1}{2} \sin^{-1}\Bigl\{ \frac{W_m}{B^{\ast}} \left( \sqrt{1-W_m^2} - \sqrt{{B^{\ast}}^2 - W_m^2} \right) \Bigr\}$$ where \(B^{\ast}\) is the shape factor $$B^{\ast} = \frac{M_x^2 - M_n^2}{M_x^2 + M_n^2}$$ and \(M_n\) and \(M_x\) are the short and long axes of the clast (Jessup et al. 2007).

Confidence Interval of the Estimate

Measurement error in \(\theta\) is handled probabilistically rather than with a fixed margin. For each clast, the probability that its true angle lies outside the critical threshold is $$p_i = \Phi\left(\frac{|\theta_i| - \theta_{c,i}}{\sigma_\theta}\right),$$ where \(\theta_{c,i}\) is the threshold at that clast's \(B^\ast\) and \(\sigma_\theta\) is angle_error. Only clasts with \(p_i \ge\) p_min are kept. Near the vertex of the hyperbola the threshold is small, so a few degrees of error can move a clast across it. Clasts with large \(B^\ast\) and uncertain classification are excluded rather than allowed to set the upper quantile.

The confidence interval is a percentile interval from a non-parametric bootstrap over clasts (n_iter resamples; after Stephan et al (2025). Measurement error enters through the classification probabilities only, so it is not added again through random perturbation of the data. Because the estimate depends on p_min, the sensitivity of the result to this choice should be reported by repeating the estimate over a range of values

References

Jessup, M. J., Law, R. D., & Frassi, C. (2007). The rigid grain net (RGN): an alternative method for estimating mean kinematic vorticity number (\(W_m\)). Journal of Structural Geology, 29(3), 411–421. doi:10.1016/j.jsg.2006.11.003

Stephan, T., Phillips, N., Tiitto, H., Perez, A., Nwakanma, M., Creaser, R., & Hollings, P. (2025). Going with the flow - Changes of vorticity control gold enrichment in Archean shear zones (Shebandowan Greenstone Belt, Superior Province, Canada). Journal of Structural Geology, 201, 105542. doi:10.1016/j.jsg.2025.105542

Examples

data(shebandowan)
set.seed(20250411)
RGN_plot(shebandowan$r, shebandowan$phi, col = "darkred", guides = TRUE, n_iter = 1e3)
